facts_from_discussion: Petitioners claimed the $23,169 of unreimbursed employee business expenses as a Schedule A itemized deduction before the 2% floor of section 67(a).
Mr. Pichardo testified that he received $7,200 ($600 per month) of vehicle reimbursements from LPS during 2016; it is unclear which reported expenses those reimbursements covered.

Mr. Pichardo testified that LPS required him to substantiate expenses beyond the $600 vehicle allowance; his testimony implied he would have had a right to reimbursement had he provided substantiation.

Petitioners offered no credible evidence as to which expenses might have been eligible for reimbursement, Mr. Pichardo did not testify that he attempted to obtain reimbursement, and petitioners did not show LPS would not have reimbursed the expenses.
Mr. Pichardo's records (a monthly-totals spreadsheet, one airline invoice, one toll invoice) did not give the amount, time, place, and business purpose of individual expenses.
The toll invoice showed $544 in tolls and $110 in fees for eight transponders but did not list Mr. Pichardo as payor and was not connected to him or his vehicle.
The Form 1098-T shows $2,250 paid for Mr. Pichardo's 2016 enrollment at UCSD Extension and states he was a 'less than half time student', which he confirmed in testimony.

The Form 1098-T was addressed to Mr. Pichardo; tuition was paid with his business credit card; no bank statements or corroborating evidence showed he personally paid the card bills; it is unclear which card expenses LPS reimbursed.
